contract: Road user a moves against the designated direction of travel of carrier region r: part of its motion runs opposite to r's designated direction. It is observed as the component of a's velocity (kin.velocity) along r's designated direction (st.lane_direction), the dot product of the velocity with the direction as a formula reads it normalised, being below minus speed_tol: the part of a's motion that runs against r's direction exceeds the speed the source cannot tell from rest. It is a state at one observation: it says nothing of whether a occupies r, of where a's body points, of the gear selected, of how long a has moved so, or of why. Not denoted: a road user at rest; one whose velocity component against r's direction is at or below speed_tol, such as one moving along r's direction or straight across it. Where r carries no designated direction, or a's velocity is unobserved, it is unknown.

params.name: speed_tol
params.meaning: the speed component at or below which motion against the direction counts as none: the source's speed resolution

elements.justification: kin.velocity: 'velocity vector', m/s, world frame; its component along the direction is a dot product.
st.lane_direction: 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in', read normalised by a formula; a place no carrier covers has none (unknown).

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: r's st.lane_direction is (1,0); a's kin.velocity is (-5,0) m/s; the component -5 m/s is below minus speed_tol.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: r's st.lane_direction is (1,0); a's kin.velocity is (5,0.2) m/s; the component is positive.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: a's kin.velocity is not observed.

contract: Road user a, moving, points to the right of the designated direction of travel of carrier region r by more than a tolerance: its heading has turned off r's direction toward the right. With h a's heading (kin.heading) and d r's designated direction (st.lane_direction), both as a formula reads them normalised, the dot product of d and h is positive, so that a points along d rather than against it, and the cross product d_x times h_y minus d_y times h_x is below minus sin_tol, so that h lies to the right of d, clockwise in the world frame, by more than the angle whose sine is sin_tol; and a's speed (kin.speed) is above speed_tol. It is a state at one observation: it says nothing of whether a occupies r, of how long its heading has been so, of the path a will follow, or of why it turns. Not denoted: a road user at rest or moving at or below speed_tol; a heading within that angle of d, or turned to its left; a heading that points against d, the dot product being at or below zero. Where r carries no designated direction, or a's heading or speed is unobserved, it is unknown.

params.name: sin_tol
params.meaning: sine of the largest angle between a's heading and r's designated direction at which a counts as keeping to that direction: the heading noise and wander the observer tolerates

params.name: speed_tol
params.meaning: the speed at or below which a counts as not moving: the source's speed resolution

elements.justification: kin.heading is the 'direction the body points', read normalised; the departure is of the body's pointing from the carrier's direction, not of a path.

st.lane_direction is the 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in', local to its carrier and unknown where none is carried, which is the reference the heading departs from.
kin.speed is the 'magnitude of velocity'; a road user at rest changes no course, so the state is read only while a moves above the tolerance.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: a moves well above speed_tol in lane r whose designated direction points east; a's heading points east-south-east, turned clockwise from r's direction by clearly more than the angle whose sine is sin_tol: the concept holds.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: a moves in r with its heading aligned with r's designated direction (cross product above minus sin_tol): the concept does not hold.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: a moves turned to the right of the lane, but the source does not observe st.lane_direction for r.

contract: Road user a is moving backward: it moves against the direction its body points. It is observed as the component of a's velocity (kin.velocity) along a's heading (kin.heading), the dot product of the velocity with the heading as a formula reads it normalised, being below minus speed_tol: the part of a's motion that runs against its heading exceeds the speed the source cannot tell from rest. It is a state at one observation: it says nothing of the gear selected, of the path a has followed or will follow, of where a is, or of why it moves so. Not denoted: a road user at rest, or one whose velocity component against its heading is at or below speed_tol; a road user moving forward. Where a's velocity or heading is unobserved, it is unknown.

params.name: speed_tol
params.meaning: the speed against the heading at or below which motion is not told from rest: the source's speed resolution

elements.span: the component of a's velocity (kin.velocity) along a's heading (kin.heading)
elements.justification: kin.velocity is the 'velocity vector' (m/s, world frame) and kin.heading the 'direction the body points' (unit vector, world frame, read normalised); their dot product is the signed speed along the heading, negative when the body moves against the way it points. kin.gear is not read: its contract says it is 'Not a stand-in for: the direction of motion — ... backing is read from kinematics'.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A car with heading (1, 0) moves with velocity (-1.5, 0) m/s: the component along its heading is -1.5 m/s, below minus speed_tol; the concept holds.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: The same car moves with velocity (2.0, 0.1) m/s: the component along its heading is positive; it is moving forward and the concept does not hold.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The car's heading is known but the source supplies no velocity at the observation; whether it moves backward is unknown.

contract: Road user a moves across the designated direction of travel of carrier region r: a is moving, its speed (kin.speed) above speed_tol, and its velocity (kin.velocity) makes with r's designated direction (st.lane_direction) an angle whose cosine, in absolute value, is at most cos_max: the absolute value of the dot product of the velocity with the normalised direction is at most cos_max times the speed. Either sense of crossing is denoted: the sign of the direction does not matter. It is a state at one observation: it says nothing of whether a occupies r, of where a began or will end its movement, or of how long it has moved so. Not denoted: a road user at rest or moving at or below speed_tol; a road user moving more nearly along r's direction than cos_max allows. Where r carries no designated direction, or a's velocity is not observed, it is unknown.

params.name: speed_tol
params.meaning: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement

params.name: cos_max
params.meaning: the largest absolute cosine between the velocity and the carrier's designated direction at which the motion counts as across the carrier

elements.justification: kin.speed: 'magnitude of velocity' (m/s); above speed_tol the road user is moving.
kin.velocity: 'velocity vector' (m/s, world frame); its dot product with the direction gives the motion along the carrier.
st.lane_direction: 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in — a lane, ... or a roadway', read normalised; a place no carrier covers has none (unknown).

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian on a lane whose direction is east walks north at 1.4 m/s: the dot product is zero, at most cos_max times the speed.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian on the same lane walks east along it at 1.4 m/s: the absolute cosine is 1, above cos_max.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian on the lane moves, but its velocity is not observed.

review_notes.text: dismissed: divergence 1 (fails_wrongly) at t=0 ms: The road user's velocity [-2.4, 14.3] has magnitude 14.5 m/s and absolute cosine exactly 0.6 with carrier direction [20, 21], meeting the inclusive threshold. … — contract: holds, body: fails; contract: "a is moving, its speed (kin.speed) above speed_tol, and its velocity (kin.velocity) makes with r's designated direction …" — The contract states its test as a dot product with "the normalised direction", and the atom contract for st.lane_direction defines that reading: the vector is the unit vector times a factor of at least 1, exactly the unit vector only where the scaled length is a whole number of micrometres. For [20, 21] that length is 29/21, which is not a whole number of micrometres, so the read vector is slightly longer than the unit vector. Under that disclosed reading, the dot product at this exact boundary (8.7 against 0.6 × 14.5) slightly exceeds cos_max times the speed, which gives the body's verdict. — "the absolute value of the dot product of the velocity with the normalised direction is at most cos_max times the speed"

contract: Road user a has turned "so as to proceed in the opposite direction": its heading has reversed, "whether accomplished by one continuous movement or not". The magnitude of its heading change over the window behind the observation (prim.heading_change over a window of length window, degrees, positive to the left) lies in the band from u_turn_min to 360 degrees minus u_turn_min, both inclusive, so that a turn short of a reversal and a full loop both lie outside it; a reversal to either hand is denoted, and one made in several movements, with halts or backing between them, is denoted where its integrated heading change lies in the band. The act begins within the window behind the observation at which it is recognized. The act is recognized at the observation at which the magnitude of the heading change over the window behind lies in that band and a's yaw rate (kin.yaw_rate) is at most yaw_tol in magnitude, where this did not hold at the previous observation: the heading has stopped turning. The concept holds at that observation only, and not again until that condition has ceased to hold and then holds again. Conduct before the window behind is not read: a reversal that takes longer than the window is not recognized. It denotes the change of a's heading only: it says nothing of the way on which a turns, of its class, of its speed, or of why it turns. Not denoted: a heading change smaller than u_turn_min, such as a turn to the left or the right; a full loop, whose heading change exceeds 360 degrees minus u_turn_min; a reversal still under way, whose yaw rate exceeds yaw_tol. Where the window is truncated or a yaw rate in it is missing, it is unknown.

params.name: window
params.meaning: the length of the window behind the observation over which the heading change is integrated: the longest duration of a reversal

params.name: u_turn_min
params.meaning: the smallest heading change magnitude at which the road user proceeds in the opposite direction: the tolerance on an exact reversal the definition leaves to the observer

params.name: yaw_tol
params.meaning: the yaw-rate magnitude at or below which the heading counts as no longer turning: the source's yaw-rate resolution

act.onset: The act begins within the window behind the observation at which it is recognized.
act.recognition: The act is recognized at the observation at which the magnitude of the heading change over the window behind lies in that band and a's yaw rate (kin.yaw_rate) is at most yaw_tol in magnitude, where this did not hold at the previous observation: the heading has stopped turning.
act.extent: The concept holds at that observation only, and not again until that condition has ceased to hold and then holds again.
act.history: Conduct before the window behind is not read: a reversal that takes longer than the window is not recognized.

elements.span: The magnitude of its heading change over the window behind the observation (prim.heading_change over a window of length window, degrees, positive to the left) lies in the band from u_turn_min to 360 degrees minus u_turn_min, both inclusive
elements.justification: prim.heading_change is 'the signed heading change (degrees, left positive) of a road user over the window behind the observation, integrated from kin.yaw_rate'; integrated through halts and backing, it measures a reversal 'whether accomplished by one continuous movement or not'; a magnitude near a half turn is proceeding 'in the opposite direction'.

elements.span: a's yaw rate (kin.yaw_rate) is at most yaw_tol in magnitude
elements.justification: kin.yaw_rate is the 'rate of change of heading'; at or below the tolerance the heading has stopped turning, which marks the reversal complete. It is not read as road curvature, its exclusion.

residues.span: the turning of a vehicle upon a highway
residues.why: The class of the road user and the place of the turn are the caller's: the concept denotes the reversal of heading for any road user anywhere, and a law reads the class and the place beside it.

literals.why: a full revolution of heading: the band's upper end is a full turn less u_turn_min, so that a full loop is not a reversal

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle reverses its heading by 180 degrees in two movements with a halt between them, within the window, then its yaw rate falls below yaw_tol; at that observation the concept holds.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle turns 90 degrees to the left; the concept does not hold.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The source does not observe the bicycle's yaw rate during its reversal.

contract: Road user a has turned "so as to proceed in the opposite direction" through region r, "whether accomplished by one continuous movement or not", recognized as it leaves r. The act begins at the observation at which a's footprint came to overlap r (rel.occupies), having not overlapped it at the previous observation: its entry into r. The act is recognized at the observation at which a's footprint does not overlap r, having overlapped it at the previous observation: its exit from r. The concept holds at that observation only, and not again until a has entered r again and left it. At that observation the magnitude of the heading change of a since its entry into r, in degrees and positive to the left, integrated from its yaw rate (kin.yaw_rate) with no interval between consecutive observations longer than step, lies in the band from u_turn_min to a full turn minus u_turn_min, both inclusive, so that a turn short of a reversal and a full loop both lie outside it; a reversal to either hand is denoted, and one made in several movements, with halts or backing between them inside r, is denoted where its integrated heading change lies in the band. Conduct before the entry is not read. It denotes the change of a's heading between its entry into r and its exit only: it says nothing of the lanes a uses, of its speed, of its class, or of why it turns. Not denoted: a passage through r whose heading change magnitude is below u_turn_min, such as a turn to the left or the right or a passage straight through; a heading change magnitude above a full turn minus u_turn_min, which is a loop; an observation at which a is still in r. Where the entry was not observed (it lies before the recording, or a's overlap with r was unknown at an observation since), where an interval between consecutive observations since the observation before the entry is longer than step, or where a yaw rate since the entry is missing, it is unknown.

params.name: step
params.meaning: the largest interval between consecutive observations across which the heading change is integrated: the sampling standard of the integration, not a window and not a bound on how long ago the entry lies

params.name: u_turn_min
params.meaning: the smallest heading change magnitude at which the passage counts as a reversal of direction: the tolerance within which an observed sampled heading counts as opposite

act.onset: The act begins at the observation at which a's footprint came to overlap r (rel.occupies), having not overlapped it at the previous observation: its entry into r.
act.recognition: The act is recognized at the observation at which a's footprint does not overlap r, having overlapped it at the previous observation: its exit from r.
act.extent: The concept holds at that observation only, and not again until a has entered r again and left it.
act.history: Conduct before the entry is not read.

elements.span: a's footprint came to overlap r (rel.occupies)
elements.justification: rel.occupies: "a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region" — its rise marks the entry into r and its fall the exit; it is footprint overlap, not distance.

kin.yaw_rate: "rate of change of heading, positive when the heading turns to the left (counter-clockwise)"; integrated by headingSince from the entry, it gives the reversal "so as to proceed in the opposite direction" whether made in one movement or not. Not a stand-in for road curvature: the road user's own turning is read.

residues.span: the turning of a vehicle upon a highway
residues.why: the class of the road user and the way it turns on are not part of the motion; the caller states the class of a and binds r on the way the words name

literals.why: a full turn of the heading: the upper end of the band is a full turn minus u_turn_min, so that a loop is told apart from a reversal

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: Region r is a roundabout region. Road user a enters r heading east, circulates counter-clockwise and leaves r heading west, its yaw rate observed at every scene at the sampling standard: the magnitude of its heading change since the entry is a half turn, inside the band, so the concept holds at the exit.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: Same region; a enters heading east and leaves heading north after a quarter turn to the left: the magnitude of its heading change is below u_turn_min, so the concept does not hold at the exit.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in holds, but a's yaw rate is missing at the scenes inside r: the heading change since the entry is unknown, and so is the concept at the exit.

review_notes.text: A tested 180-degree passage lasting longer than step, with every sampling interval equal to step, holds in both the contract and the body; step does not limit the total passage duration.
A tested 180-degree turn completed at entry, followed by zero heading change through exit, fails in both the contract and the body; the pre-entry turn is not counted.

contract: The road user is at rest at the observation — "complete cessation from movement" — observed as its speed (kin.speed) at or below a tolerance the caller sets for the source's speed resolution. It denotes a state at one observation: it says nothing of how long the road user stays at rest, where it is, or why. Not denoted: a slowing whose sampled speed stays above the tolerance.

params.name: speed_tol
params.meaning: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution

elements.span: its speed (kin.speed) at or below a tolerance
elements.justification: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' in m/s; an absolute cessation is observed over sampled speeds only within the caller's tolerance. Its exclusion of acceleration does not apply.

residues.why: the scope of the definition (a stop that a law requires) is decided by the law that calls the concept, not by the state observed

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A vehicle's sampled speed is at the tolerance or below.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: A vehicle creeps forward with a sampled speed above the tolerance.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The source does not observe the road user's speed.

contract: Road user a travels clockwise about the reference point of region r, as seen from above: the point lies to the right of a's direction of travel and a's velocity turns about it clockwise. It is observed with a's position (kin.position), a's velocity (kin.velocity), a's speed (kin.speed) and r's reference point (st.region_geometry), in the world frame, in which a turn to the left is counter-clockwise (the frame of kin.yaw_rate): with d the vector from r's reference point to a's position, the cross product of d with a's velocity is negative, and its square exceeds sin_tol squared times the squared length of d times the square of a's speed, so that the share of a's motion that turns about the point is above sin_tol; and a's speed is above speed_tol. It is a state at one observation: it says nothing of whether a occupies r, of the path a followed before, or of why a moves so. Not denoted: a road user at rest or moving at or below speed_tol; one travelling counter-clockwise about the point; one moving towards or away from the point within the angle sin_tol allows; one at the point itself. Where r's reference point, a's position or a's velocity is unobserved, it is unknown.

params.name: speed_tol
params.meaning: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement

params.name: sin_tol
params.meaning: the share of the speed, across the line to the reference point, at or below which motion counts as towards or away from the point rather than around it

elements.justification: kin.position: 'position of the body's reference point', world frame; the vector from r's reference point to it is d.
kin.velocity: 'velocity vector', world frame; its cross product with d gives the sense of travel about the point.
kin.speed: 'magnitude of velocity'; it bounds the share of the motion turning about the point and excludes a road user at rest.

st.region_geometry: 'the reference point and the boundary polygon of a structure region in the world frame'; the reference point is the point travel is judged about. Not a stand-in for occupancy: the concept reads no footprint.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: The region is mapped with its reference point and a boundary polygon around that point (a small central island, every scene's structure carrying both). A car moves around the region outside its boundary, keeping the reference point on its right, its velocity mostly across the line to the point and its speed well above speed_tol.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: The region is mapped as in holds, with its reference point and a boundary polygon. A car moves around the region outside its boundary keeping the reference point on its left (counter-clockwise).

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The region is mapped as in holds, with its reference point and a boundary polygon, and the car moves as in holds, but the source does not observe the car's motion: its velocity and its speed are declared absent, while its position and the region's geometry are observed.

contract: Road user a has made a turn to the right through region r, recognized as it leaves r. The act begins at the observation at which a's footprint came to overlap r (rel.occupies), having not overlapped it at the previous observation: its entry into r. The act is recognized at the observation at which a's footprint does not overlap r, having overlapped it at the previous observation: its exit from r. The concept holds at that observation only, and not again until a has entered r again and left it. At that observation the heading change of a since its entry into r, in degrees and positive to the left, integrated from its yaw rate (kin.yaw_rate) with no interval between consecutive observations longer than step, lies in the band from minus u_turn_min exclusive to minus turn_min inclusive: a turn to the right by at least turn_min and by less than u_turn_min, so that a passage whose heading changes too little to be a turn and a reversal of direction both lie outside it. Conduct before the entry is not read. It denotes the change of a's heading between its entry into r and its exit only: it says nothing of the lanes a uses, of its speed, of its class, or of why it turns. Not denoted: a passage through r whose heading change is above minus turn_min, such as one straight through or a turn to the left; a heading change of minus u_turn_min or less, which is a reversal of direction; an observation at which a is still in r. Where the entry was not observed (it lies before the recording, or a's overlap with r was unknown at an observation since), where an interval between consecutive observations since the observation before the entry is longer than step, or where a yaw rate since the entry is missing, it is unknown.

params.name: step
params.meaning: the largest interval between consecutive observations across which the heading change is integrated: the sampling standard of the integration, not a window and not a bound on how long ago the entry lies

params.name: turn_min
params.meaning: the smallest heading change to the right between entry and exit at which the passage counts as a turn rather than a passage straight through

params.name: u_turn_min
params.meaning: the smallest heading change magnitude at which the passage counts as a reversal of direction rather than a turn

act.onset: The act begins at the observation at which a's footprint came to overlap r (rel.occupies), having not overlapped it at the previous observation: its entry into r.
act.recognition: The act is recognized at the observation at which a's footprint does not overlap r, having overlapped it at the previous observation: its exit from r.
act.extent: The concept holds at that observation only, and not again until a has entered r again and left it.
act.history: Conduct before the entry is not read.

elements.span: a's footprint came to overlap r (rel.occupies)
elements.justification: rel.occupies: "a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region" — its rise marks the entry into r and its fall the exit; it is footprint overlap, not distance.

kin.yaw_rate: "rate of change of heading, positive when the heading turns to the left (counter-clockwise)"; integrated by headingSince from the entry, a negative change is a turn to the right. Not a stand-in for road curvature: the road user's own turning is read.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: Region r is a roundabout region. Road user a approaches heading east with zero yaw rate and enters r. At each scene from the one after its entry up to and including its exit it turns to the right at a constant yaw rate, and its heading at every scene is consistent with that rate: the heading at a scene is the heading at the previous scene turned by the yaw rate observed at that scene times the interval since the previous scene (a rate at a scene covers the interval before it), so the heading goes from east through intermediate directions to south and is never held while the rate is non-zero. Every interval between scenes is within the sampling standard. At its exit, heading south, its integrated heading change since the entry is a quarter turn to the right, inside the band, so the concept holds at the exit, the observation at which it is judged.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: Same region; a enters heading east and leaves heading east again after passing straight through, its heading unchanged and its yaw rate zero at every scene, consistent with each other: its heading change since the entry is zero, above minus turn_min, so the concept does not hold at the exit, the observation at which it is judged.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in holds, with the same positions and the same headings turning from east to south between the entry and the exit, but a's yaw rate is not observed: the heading change since the entry is unknown, and so is the concept at the exit.

contract: Road user a, occupying lane r1, begins to move into lane r2, the neighbouring lane of the same direction on side s of r1 (s left or right): the event of a's footprint first reaching into r2 from r1. It is observed with a's footprint occupancy (rel.occupies) and the lanes' adjacency (st.lane_adjacency): r2 is r1's neighbour on side s, a's footprint overlaps both r1 and r2 at the observation, and at the previous observation it overlapped r1 and did not overlap r2. The event is recognized at the first observation at which a's footprint overlaps r2, and conduct before the previous observation is not read. The concept holds at that observation only, and not again until a's footprint has ceased to overlap r2 and again comes to overlap it from r1. It says nothing of whether a completes the move, of its signal, of its speed, or of why it moves. Not denoted: a road user that comes into r2 from elsewhere than r1; one that stays within r1; a lane r2 that is not r1's neighbour of the same direction on side s, such as an opposing lane. Where a's overlap with either lane at the observation or at the previous one is unobserved, where there is no previous observation, or where the adjacency of the two lanes is not observed, it is unknown.

elements.justification: rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'; read for a with r1 and with r2, at the observation and at the previous one.

st.lane_adjacency: 'left / right neighbouring lane of the same direction'; read as r2 being r1's neighbour on side s. Its exclusion ('not a stand-in for: the marking between two lanes') does not apply: no marking is read.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: Two adjacent lanes of the same direction; r2 is recorded as r1's left neighbour (and r1 as r2's right neighbour), looking along their common direction; s is left. At the observation before the judged one, a's footprint lies wholly inside r1, clear of r2. At the judged observation, a's footprint straddles the line between r1 and r2 and overlaps both. The scenario is judged at that observation only, which has a previous observation in the trace.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: Same lanes, adjacency and s as holds. a's footprint lies wholly inside r1, clear of r2, at the judged observation and at the previous one. The scenario is judged at that observation only, which has a previous observation in the trace.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Same trace, lanes, adjacency and s as holds, judged at the same observation, with a's footprint occupancy unobserved: whether a overlaps r1 or r2 at the judged observation and at the previous one is not known.

act.extent: The concept holds at that observation only, and not again until a has entered r again and left it.
act.history: Conduct before the entry is not read.

elements.span: a's footprint came to overlap r (rel.occupies)
elements.justification: rel.occupies: "a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region" — its rise marks the entry into r and its fall the exit; it is footprint overlap, not distance, so neither nearness nor geometry stands for it.

kin.yaw_rate: "rate of change of heading, positive when the heading turns to the left (counter-clockwise)"; the formula language's heading change since a formula last became true (headingSince, onset the rise of the overlap with r) integrates it. Not a stand-in for road curvature: the concept reads the road user's own turning, not the road's.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: Region r is an intersection region. Road user a, observed at every scene at the sampling standard, enters r heading east with a yaw rate of zero up to and including the entry observation; from the next observation on it carries a constant yaw rate to the left, and its heading at every scene is the heading of the scene before turned by that scene's yaw rate held over the interval before it (so the trace is one an adapter produces: heading and yaw rate agree at every scene, passing through intermediate, non-axis headings), until it has turned a quarter turn to the left and leaves r heading north. At the exit observation its heading change since the entry, a quarter turn, lies in the band, so the concept holds there.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: Same region; the mirror image of holds: a enters r heading east with a yaw rate of zero up to and including the entry, then carries a constant yaw rate to the right, its heading at every scene agreeing with the yaw rate held over the interval before that scene, and leaves r heading south after a quarter turn to the right: the heading change since the entry is negative, below turn_min, so the concept does not hold at the exit.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in holds, the same positions and headings, but the source supplies no yaw rate for a at any scene: the heading change since the entry cannot be integrated and the concept is unknown at the exit.

review_notes.text: The body agreed with the contract on both tested passages: a fully observed 90-degree left turn and the same entry-to-exit change preceded by a right turn before entry. Neither test established a defect.

contract: Road user a is parked: "the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not", observed as a at rest at every observation of the window behind the observation, of length min_duration: at each of them a's speed (kin.speed, read through drv.motion.complete_halt) is at or below speed_tol. A halt shorter than min_duration, which may be the temporary halt the definition leaves out, is not denoted. It denotes a state at one observation: it says nothing of whether a rider is on a, of where a stands, or of why it stands. Not denoted: a road user whose speed was above speed_tol at some observation of that window. Where the window reaches before the start of the recording or a speed in it is unobserved, it is unknown.

params.name: speed_tol
params.meaning: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution

params.name: min_duration
params.meaning: the length of the window behind over which the road user must have been at rest: the longest halt that still counts as a temporary one

elements.span: a at rest at every observation of the window behind the observation, of length min_duration
elements.justification: drv.motion.complete_halt: 'The road user is at rest at the observation ... observed as its speed (kin.speed) at or below a tolerance the caller sets'; holding it at every observation of a window behind (holdsFor over time) is the standing the definition names, 'whether occupied or not', so no occupancy is read.

residues.span: otherwise than temporarily for the purpose of and while actually engaged in loading or unloading of merchandise or passengers
residues.why: a purpose is not observable; the definition's exclusion of a temporary halt is read only by the halt's duration (min_duration): a halt held longer than min_duration while loading is denoted, a halt shorter than it for any purpose is not

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle stands at rest beside the curb at every observation of the window behind, with no rider on it.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle halts briefly and moves off again within the window behind: its speed is above the tolerance at some observation of the window.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The source supplies no speed for the bicycle during the window.

review_notes.text: The harness requires consecutive observations in a look-back window to be at most half the window's length apart. The contract states no sampling-gap limit, but the harness rejected the sparse-window example as incomplete, so no divergence was confirmed.
The boundary test agreed with the contract: a speed above tolerance exactly min_duration before the current observation makes the body fail.

contract: Road user a has completed a turn to the left. Its heading change over the window behind the observation (prim.heading_change over a window of length window, degrees, positive to the left) lies in the band from turn_min inclusive to u_turn_min exclusive, so that a heading change too small to be a turn and a reversal of direction both lie outside it. The act begins within the window behind the observation at which it is recognized. The act is recognized at the observation at which the heading change over the window behind lies in that band and a's yaw rate (kin.yaw_rate) is at most yaw_tol in magnitude, where this did not hold at the previous observation: the heading has stopped turning. The concept holds at that observation only, and not again until that condition has ceased to hold and then holds again. Conduct before the window behind is not read: a turn that takes longer than the window is not recognized. It denotes the change of a's heading only: it says nothing of the lane, the intersection or the way on which a turns, of its speed, or of why it turns. Not denoted: a heading change to the left smaller than turn_min, such as a lane change or a drift; a heading change of u_turn_min or more, which is a reversal of direction; a turn to the right; a turn still under way, whose yaw rate exceeds yaw_tol. Where the window is truncated or a yaw rate in it is missing, it is unknown.

params.name: window
params.meaning: the length of the window behind the observation over which the heading change is integrated: the longest duration of a turn

params.name: turn_min
params.meaning: the smallest heading change that is a turn

params.name: u_turn_min
params.meaning: the smallest heading change that is a reversal of direction, which bounds the band of a turn from above

params.name: yaw_tol
params.meaning: the yaw-rate magnitude at or below which the heading counts as no longer turning: the source's yaw-rate resolution

act.onset: The act begins within the window behind the observation at which it is recognized.
act.recognition: The act is recognized at the observation at which the heading change over the window behind lies in that band and a's yaw rate (kin.yaw_rate) is at most yaw_tol in magnitude, where this did not hold at the previous observation: the heading has stopped turning.
act.extent: The concept holds at that observation only, and not again until that condition has ceased to hold and then holds again.
act.history: Conduct before the window behind is not read: a turn that takes longer than the window is not recognized.

elements.span: Its heading change over the window behind the observation (prim.heading_change over a window of length window, degrees, positive to the left) lies in the band from turn_min inclusive to u_turn_min exclusive
elements.justification: prim.heading_change is 'the signed heading change (degrees, left positive) of a road user over the window behind the observation, integrated from kin.yaw_rate; unknown where the window is truncated, sampled too sparsely, or a yaw rate is missing'; a positive value in the band from turn_min to u_turn_min is a turn to the left, and a negative value, a turn to the right, lies outside it.

elements.span: a's yaw rate (kin.yaw_rate) is at most yaw_tol in magnitude
elements.justification: kin.yaw_rate is the 'rate of change of heading, positive when the heading turns to the left (counter-clockwise)'; at or below the tolerance in magnitude the heading has stopped turning, which marks the turn complete. It is not read as road curvature, its exclusion: it is the road user's own heading change.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle riding straight turns to the left at a constant yaw rate for 6 s, 90 degrees in total, then rides straight with zero yaw rate; the trace is observed at a steady interval from well before the window behind the recognition, and the bicycle's heading at every observation is its heading at the observation before turned by the yaw rate of this observation times the interval between them, so that heading and yaw rate agree. At the first observation with zero yaw rate after the turn, the heading change over the window behind is 90 degrees and the concept holds.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle changes lane to the left: its yaw rate is positive for a few observations, turning its heading 10 degrees to the left, then negative for as many, turning it back; its heading at every observation is its heading at the observation before turned by the yaw rate of this observation times the interval between them. Over every covered window the heading change stays at or below 10 degrees, below turn_min, and the concept does not hold.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The holds trace, but the source does not observe the bicycle's yaw rate: at the observation where the turn would be recognized, neither the heading change over the window behind nor the yaw rate is known, and the concept is unknown.

differs_from.why: drv.motion.u_turn denotes a reversal of direction to either hand: the magnitude of the heading change lies from u_turn_min to 360 degrees minus u_turn_min. This concept denotes a turn to the left only: the signed heading change, left positive, lies from turn_min inclusive to u_turn_min exclusive, so a reversal, which u_turn denotes, and a turn to the right are excluded here, and a left turn short of a reversal, which this concept denotes, is excluded from u_turn. The two notions are disjoint and neither can be stated through the other.

review_notes.text: dismissed: divergence 1 (holds_wrongly) at t=6000 ms: A continuous leftward turn is already under way at t=0 and is still under way at t=4000 ms; the first stopped observation is t=6000 ms. The act began before the … — contract: fails, body: holds; contract: "The act begins within the window behind the observation at which it is recognized." — The contract says conduct before the window is not read, and states the recognition condition in terms of the window alone. In the executed facts that condition holds at t=6000 ms and did not hold at t=4000 ms: yaw rate 30 deg/s at 2000 and 4000 ms gives an in-band heading change, then yaw rate 0 at 6000 ms. A reasonable reading therefore treats the recognized act as the turning within the window, so it begins there, and gives the body's verdict. — "Conduct before the window behind is not read"

contract: Road user a overtakes and passes road user b from the rear: a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it. b is ahead of a where the longitudinal component of b's bearing in a's frame, the component along a's heading (kin.heading) of the vector from a's position to b's position (kin.position), is positive and the two bodies' projections on a's heading share no length (rel.longitudinal_overlap negative); b is behind a where that component is negative and the projections share no length. The act begins at the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of a with their headings aligned within same_dir_cos (rel.same_direction). The act is recognized at the observation at which b is behind a and was not behind a at the previous observation, where b was ahead of a with headings aligned at some observation of the window behind. The concept holds at that observation only, and not again until b has again been ahead of a and then comes to be behind it. Conduct before the window behind is not read: a pass that takes longer than the window is not recognized. It denotes the relative motion of the two road users only: it says nothing of the lanes they occupy, of whether b moves, or of why a passes. Not denoted: a drawing alongside b that does not clear b; b ahead of a only while their headings are not aligned (a road user met head-on or crossing); b behind a at every observation of the window. Where the positions of a and b are unobserved, it is unknown.

params.name: window
params.meaning: the longest duration of a pass the concept recognizes: how far behind the observation it looks for b ahead of a

params.name: same_dir_cos
params.meaning: cosine of the largest heading difference at which a and b count as travelling in the same direction

act.onset: The act begins at the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of a with their headings aligned within same_dir_cos (rel.same_direction).
act.recognition: The act is recognized at the observation at which b is behind a and was not behind a at the previous observation, where b was ahead of a with headings aligned at some observation of the window behind.
act.extent: The concept holds at that observation only, and not again until b has again been ahead of a and then comes to be behind it.
act.history: Conduct before the window behind is not read: a pass that takes longer than the window is not recognized.

elements.span: the component along a's heading (kin.heading) of the vector from a's position to b's position (kin.position)
elements.justification: kin.position: 'position of the body's reference point' (m, world frame); kin.heading: 'direction the body points; a formula reads it normalised ... the unit vector times a factor of at least 1', so the sign of the dot product of a's heading with the vector from a's position to b's position is the sign of the longitudinal component of b's direction from a in a's frame (rel.bearing: 'direction of b from a in a's frame'). It is written over the kinematics the relation is 'Computed from' (§7), so that unobserved positions leave it unknown rather than a relation derived regardless of the manifest. Only its sign is read: positive for b ahead of a, negative for b behind.

elements.span: the two bodies' projections on a's heading share no length (rel.longitudinal_overlap negative)
elements.justification: rel.longitudinal_overlap: 'the length the two footprints' projections on that axis share, negative for the gap between the projections'; a negative value means the bodies are not side by side, so a has cleared b (or not yet reached it). Used as a projection, not as a contact or a distance.

elements.span: with their headings aligned within same_dir_cos (rel.same_direction)
elements.justification: rel.same_direction: 'headings aligned: the cosine of the angle between the headings is above its tolerance', with the tolerance same_dir_cos; it tells an overtaking from a meeting or a crossing.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: a follows b in the same lane 15 m behind at 12 m/s while b is halted; a moves to the adjacent lane, draws alongside and, 4 s after b was last ahead of it, has b 3 m behind it: at that observation the concept holds.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: a follows b, moves to the adjacent lane and draws alongside b, then halts with the two bodies still side by side; b never comes to be behind a within the window.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: a draws past b in the adjacent lane as in holds, but the positions of the road users are not observed, so whether b is ahead of or behind a cannot be told.

review_notes.text: Tested a pass recognized one second after the recording begins, within a two-second window. The observed aligned-ahead and first-behind observations suffice: the body holds, agreeing with the contract despite the truncated history.

contract: Road user a, moving, points to the left of the designated direction of travel of carrier region r by more than a tolerance: its heading has turned off r's direction toward the left. With h a's heading (kin.heading) and d r's designated direction (st.lane_direction), both as a formula reads them normalised, the dot product of d and h is positive, so that a points along d rather than against it, and the cross product d_x times h_y minus d_y times h_x is above sin_tol, so that h lies to the left of d, counter-clockwise in the world frame, by more than the angle whose sine is sin_tol; and a's speed (kin.speed) is above speed_tol. It is a state at one observation: it says nothing of whether a occupies r, of how long its heading has been so, of the path a will follow, or of why it turns. Not denoted: a road user at rest or moving at or below speed_tol; a heading within that angle of d, or turned to its right; a heading that points against d, the dot product being at or below zero. Where r carries no designated direction, or a's heading or speed is unobserved, it is unknown.

params.name: sin_tol
params.meaning: sine of the largest angle between a's heading and r's designated direction at which a counts as keeping r's direction

params.name: speed_tol
params.meaning: the speed at or below which a counts as at rest, so that its heading marks no course

elements.justification: kin.heading: 'direction the body points', read normalised as the contract states.
st.lane_direction: 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in'; a carrier with none reads unknown, as the contract states.
kin.speed: 'magnitude of velocity'; a road user at rest has no course to depart from.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: r's direction points along x; a moves at 10 m/s with its heading turned about ten degrees counter-clockwise from x: dot positive, cross above sin_tol.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: r's direction points along x; a moves at 10 m/s with its heading turned about ten degrees clockwise from x: the cross product is negative.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As holds, but a's heading is not observed on the source.

differs_from.why: It denotes the mirror state: a heading turned to the LEFT of the carrier's direction (cross product d_x*h_y - d_y*h_x above +sin_tol), which the accepted concept's contract explicitly excludes ('Not denoted: ... a heading within that angle of d, or turned to its left'). Its formals cannot be swapped or negated to obtain this side (track and region formals; no sign formal), and a literal side formal would be read only where a spelling is expected, so the two sides are separate concepts. A law that requires a signal to the side of a course change needs both.

contract: Road user a overtakes and passes road user b on b's right: a overtakes and passes b from the rear, as drv.interaction.overtake_pass states it with the same window and the same heading tolerance, and makes the passage with b on its left. b is on a's left where the lateral component of b's bearing in a's frame (rel.bearing) is positive; the two are side by side where their projections on a's heading share length (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero). b is ahead of a where the longitudinal component, along a's heading (kin.heading), of the vector from a's position to b's position (kin.position) is positive and the two bodies' projections on a's heading share no length (rel.longitudinal_overlap negative); their headings are aligned where the cosine of the angle between them is above same_dir_cos (rel.same_direction). The act begins at the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of a with their headings aligned within same_dir_cos. The act is recognized at the observation at which drv.interaction.overtake_pass holds for a and b, where b is on a's left there and at every observation since the act began at which the two are side by side. The concept holds at that observation only, and not again until b has again been ahead of a and then comes to be behind it. Conduct before the window behind is not read: a pass that takes longer than the window is not recognized. It denotes the relative motion of the two road users and the side on which a passes only: it says nothing of the lanes or the pavement a uses, of whether b moves, or of why a passes. Not denoted: a pass with b on a's right at the recognition or at some observation at which the two are side by side, which is a pass on b's left; a drawing alongside b that does not clear b; b ahead of a only while their headings are not aligned. Where b's bearing, the positions or headings of a and b, or the overlap of the two bodies is unobserved at an observation the passage reads, it is unknown.

params.name: window
params.meaning: the longest duration of the pass, from having b ahead to having it behind; conduct before the window is not read

params.name: same_dir_cos
params.meaning: cosine of the largest heading difference at which a and b count as travelling in the same direction

act.onset: The act begins at the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of a with their headings aligned within same_dir_cos.
act.recognition: The act is recognized at the observation at which drv.interaction.overtake_pass holds for a and b, where b is on a's left there and at every observation since the act began at which the two are side by side.
act.extent: The concept holds at that observation only, and not again until b has again been ahead of a and then comes to be behind it.
act.history: Conduct before the window behind is not read: a pass that takes longer than the window is not recognized.

elements.span: a overtakes and passes b from the rear, as drv.interaction.overtake_pass states it with the same window and the same heading tolerance
elements.justification: The pass from the rear and its recognition are those of drv.interaction.overtake_pass, whose contract denotes 'Road user a overtakes and passes road user b from the rear: a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it'; this concept adds only the side, so it calls that concept with its own window and same_dir_cos rather than rebuilding it.

elements.span: b is on a's left where the lateral component of b's bearing in a's frame (rel.bearing) is positive
elements.justification: rel.bearing is the 'direction of b from a in a's frame (for "on the right of", "immediately to the rear")': its lateral component tells on which side of a the other road user lies, which is the side of the passage.

elements.span: the two are side by side where their projections on a's heading share length (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero)
elements.justification: rel.longitudinal_overlap: 'the bodies overlap along the subject's heading (side by side): the length the two footprints' projections on that axis share'; its exclusion (neither a contact nor a distance between the bodies) does not apply, since only the side-by-side phase of the pass is read with it.

elements.span: b is ahead of a where the longitudinal component, along a's heading (kin.heading), of the vector from a's position to b's position (kin.position) is positive and the two bodies' projections on a's heading share no length (rel.longitudinal_overlap negative)
elements.justification: The onset from which the side-by-side observations are counted is the one drv.interaction.overtake_pass states, so 'ahead' is read as that concept reads it: kin.position is the 'position of the body's reference point' and kin.heading the 'direction the body points', so the component along a's heading of the vector between the positions orders the two along a's heading; rel.longitudinal_overlap, 'negative for the gap between the projections', says the bodies are not side by side.

elements.span: their headings are aligned where the cosine of the angle between them is above same_dir_cos (rel.same_direction)
elements.justification: rel.same_direction: 'headings aligned: the cosine of the angle between the headings is above its tolerance, which is the cosine of the largest angle allowed'; same_dir_cos is that tolerance, the same one passed to drv.interaction.overtake_pass, and it marks the act's onset.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: a follows b in the same lane with headings aligned within same_dir_cos (rel.same_direction), b ahead of a along a's heading with no longitudinal overlap; a moves to the right, draws alongside with b's bearing lateral component positive (b on a's left) while rel.longitudinal_overlap is non-negative, and comes to have b behind it with b still on its left, all within the window: the concept holds at the observation at which b first is behind a.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: The same pass made with a moving to the left: while side by side, b's bearing lateral component is negative (b on a's right), and at recognition b is behind a on its right: drv.interaction.overtake_pass holds but the passage is on b's left, so the concept does not hold.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The pass of the holds scenario with rel.bearing not observed on the source: drv.interaction.overtake_pass, read from the positions, headings and overlap, holds at the observation at which b first is behind a, but the side on which b lies there and while the two are side by side cannot be read, so the concept is unknown.

review_notes.text: Tested a one-second right-side pass with window = 2 s and a recording beginning at its aligned-ahead onset. The body holds at recognition despite the shorter recording, agreeing with the contract; this is not a divergence.
